Anchr is helping supply chain teams connect their operations. Credit: Getty
Smayan Mehra, Co-Founder at anchr, explains how the company is delivering strong solutions to drive efficient end-to-end supply chain operations
Supply chain technology has come a long way in recent years, as AI, automation and predictive analytics have proven to be critical tools to meet demand.
Many new tools require organisations to completely overhaul their internal systems, being unable to adapt to their existing ERPs.
anchr, however,
sits on top of existing ERPs
to help food distributors transform their operations.
Breaking down silos
anchr focuses on developing an
agentic workforce for supply chain
operations, using its AI tools to unify sales, operations, inventory, logistics and finance into a singular layer. Through this, businesses are able to transform fragmented data points into actionable insights, with real-time visibility and guided insights to help teams as they reduce waste, execute faster and align daily work.
The platform is specifically designed to help businesses that buy, move and sell physical products, understanding the issues that come with these workflows.
It connects orders, purchasing, finance and fulfilment across pre-existing systems, meaning that teams do not have to spend time and money on learning new solutions. This effective method works for the teams, making their operations more efficient so they can meet demand faster.
anchr was formed in order to tackle some of the main issues within the food industry, as extended manual tasks were increasingly causing delays. In the food industry, everything needs to be delivered in a timely manner, with specific needs of safety checks and temperature control.
Food distributors are a critical part of the food supply chain, but it has run on fragmented software, manual workflows and outdated systems. As the industry becomes more complex – an ageing population and workforce, alongside growing food demand, instability within crops and inflation – these systems are adding more pressure to an already struggling industry.
Across the food and drink industry, it helps with temperature-controlled and time-sensitive food distribution, as well as the
high-volume movement of beverages and snacks
Since its foundation, the platform has also ventured into other industries, following the success of its rollout.
“We are building the first end-to-end AI operating system for supply chains, designed to automate the tedious back-office work that has burdened this industry for far too long. We don't just go end-to-end, we provide a truly bespoke solution,” explains Smayan Mehra, Co-Founder at anchr.
Tzar Taraporvala and Smayan Mehra, Founders of Anchr. Credit: Anchr

anchr finds that executives spend more than 20 hours a week on unstructured data analysis
Finance teams lose 1,000+ hours to manual reconciliation every year
With anchr, finance teams can see a 20% improvement to collection-email response rate
Gut-driven buying results in 5% purchasing error rate
Sales teams can see a US$350K annual productivity gain with anchr
Workforce agents
anchr provides an AI employee for every operational team, using a shared workforce to meet demands of each department.
Within sales, teams can turn each inbound request into a complete and accurate order. This helps reduce time spent processing orders and more time developing customer relationships. It finds relevant add-ons using account history and availability in order to drive basket opportunities.
Purchasing teams are seeing greater anticipation of demand, resulting in better supplier decisions and completed orders. Through anchr, teams can continuously connect inventory, demand, receipts and coverage. It also allows better risk identification, working to prevent shortages and find cover when they do occur. title: DP World Strengthens FMCG Logistics Capabilities in Europe
content:
DP World Strengthens FMCG Logistics Capabilities in Europe
Prioritise Us
on Google
DP World has launched its first Fast Moving Consumer Goods Contract Logistics operation in Italy. Credit: DP World
Rainer Schmid, CCO of DP World Europe explains how its first FMCG Contract Logistics operation in Italy strengthens its ability to meet customer demand
DP World has announced the launch of its first Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) Contract Logistics operation in Italy, working to meet customer demand at greater efficiency.
The facility will operate across the food and beverage industry, as well as consumer goods and ecommerce, fulfilling the needs of a range of customers.
This is a demonstration of DP World’s growing presence in Europe, as it strengthens its capabilities and global reach.
Market capabilities
DP World is expanding its European presence as a reliable and capable logistics partner. It is entering one of Europe’s largest consumer and manufacturing markets, while presenting itself as a strong option for Contract Logistics within the food and beverage sector.
The company has opened a 22,000m² temperature-controlled, multi-customer facility near Bologna. The variety within the facility means it can support the movement of a range of goods, including food and beverages which need to be stored and transported at specific temperatures to avoid spoilage.
The facility, at Castel San Pietro Terme, will combine warehousing, transport ecommerce fulfilment and
value-added logistics services
. In doing this, DP World is offering integrated, end-to-end supply chain solutions for customers across Europe, but particularly in Italy.
“Launching our first FMCG Contract Logistics operation in Italy is an important milestone for DP World,” explains Rainer Schmid, CCO of DP World Europe.
Rainer Schmid, CCO of DP World Europe
“Italy is a key European market, and expanding our capabilities here strengthens our network while opening new opportunities in the food and beverage sector.”
At a glance
DP World is opening a 22,000 m² temperature-controlled, multi-customer facility
It is providing integrated, end-to-end supply chain solutions through warehousing, transport, ecommerce fulfilment and value-added logistics
The new facility includes temperature-controlled storage at 18–20°C
The operation has approximately 30,000 pallet positions
It aims to help organisations grow
Supply chain partnerships
The operation is taking place through a strategic partnership with Alce Nero. The Italian organic food company is the site’s anchor customer, and is looking to undergo resilient supply chain growth.
Within the partnership, DP World is taking on a management role of some of Alce Nero’s logistics operations, including warehousing, ecommerce fulfilment and transportation. This allows the company to grow its core business operations and focus on future growth plans, rather than navigating a complex logistics market.
Rainer continues, “Our partnership with Alce Nero is a strong example of how we want to grow: by starting with a customer need, building the right solution around it and creating capabilities that can then support other businesses in the market.”
The world of logistics has become increasingly complex, with geopolitical events happening every week. Trade relationships are constantly changing, climate events are proving a disruptor across crop yield, transportation capabilities and more.
At the same time, growing digitalisation efforts are increasing vulnerability to cyber attacks, as organisations are not undertaking sufficient safety measures.
Volatility is growing
, meaning logistics partners need to prove they can be reliable. DP World’s new facility aims to connect Europe in a much more reliable and efficient way.
DP World plays a vital role in keeping global trade moving by connecting economies, industries and businesses worldwide. Credit: DP World
Italy is a key European market, and expanding our capabilities here strengthens our network while opening new opportunities in the food and beverage sector.
Rainer Schmid, CCO of DP World Europe
Meeting customer needs
The facility is supporting Alce Nero with its temperature-controlled storage capabilities, sitting at 18–20°C. It also has organic product handling capabilities and integrated logistics technology in order to support a range of consumables businesses.
Alongside this, it can support customers in ecommerce, consumer goods and technology, navigating several types of supply chain and demonstrating its flexibility in logistics support.
The multi-customer operation has approximately 30,000 pallet positions and the capacity to support additional customers, meaning DP World is intending to grow and support its customers’ growth.
As it is near Bologna, it has easy access to Italy’s domestic market and major European transport corridors. This further supports its capabilities for growth and
meeting customer demand
“We are very pleased with the launch of our partnership with DP World. Finding the right logistics partner was an important process for Alce Nero, given the complexity of our business model, which brings together different supply chains, members, partners and customers across multiple channels, each with specific requirements and logistics flows,” says Renzo Patelli, General Manager at Alce Nero Spa.
Alce Nero has a wide range of products, which DP World will be supporting with. Credit: Alce Nero
“This partnership gives us a more integrated approach to managing that complexity and will help make our logistics operations more efficient, flexible and responsive as we pursue further growth in Italy and internationally. It will also allow us to focus even more closely on our core business: producing and bringing to market high-quality organic food that reflects the values that have always guided Alce Nero.”
As DP World expands, the company is strengthening its European network in order to better serve customers with end-to-end supply chain solutions.
Key companies
DP World
DP World is a leading global supply chain and logistics company based in Dubai, UAE. Operating across six continents with 295 terminals, it handles roughly 10% of global container traffic. Founded in 2005, DP World provides integrated logistics solutions including port operations, cargo handling, and maritime services. The company employs over 100,000 people worldwide and continues expanding through strategic acquisitions.
Alce Nero Spa
Alce Nero is an Italian organic food company founded in 1978, specializing in organic agricultural products. The cooperative unites over 1,000 organic farmers across Italy who cultivate without synthetic chemicals or GMOs. Alce Nero produces pasta, tomato sauces, olive oil, and fruit juices. The brand emphasizes sustainability, biodiversity, and fair farmer compensation while maintaining strict organic certification standards throughout its chain.

title: Toyota updates the 2027 RAV4 PHEV with an NACS port and up to 52 miles of EV range
content:

The 2027
RAV4 is bringing a few major updates, including an added NACS charge port on all plug-in hybrid (PHEV) models.
2027 Toyota RAV4 prices and updates
The RAV4 was Toyota’s best-selling nameplate in the US last year and consistently ranks among America’s most popular vehicles alongside the Ford F-Series and Chevrolet Silverado.
For the 2027 model year, Toyota added several notable upgrades. The 2027 Toyota RAV4 will be available with hybrid (HEV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains, with available front- or all-wheel drive (AWD).
The biggest change is that all 2027 RAV4 PHEV models now have a built-in NACS charge port with Level 3 DC fast-charging capabilities.
The NACS port is on the driver’s side and lets drivers use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. All PHEV grades also include an 11 kW onboard AC charger.
Powered by Toyota’s sixth-generation PHEV system, the plug-in RAV4 has standard AWD with a combined output of 321 horsepower. The setup includes a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine, two electric motors, and a high-capacity traction battery.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV Woodland (Source: Toyota)
The 2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV offers up to 52 miles of pure electric range on the base SE trim. It will be available in four trims: SE, XSE, Woodland, and GR Sport.
Toyota updated the suspension system in the Woodland grade for the 2027 model year with new springs, shocks, and jounce bumpers, giving it 9.1″ of ground clearance.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV GR-Sport (Source: Toyota)
The Woodland trim adds a rugged look with standard All-Terrain tires, Roof Rails with Cross Bars, and a Tow Hitch Receiver. It also features new all-weather floor and cargo mats.
Lastly, the RAV4 GR Sport trim is for those who want a more performance-oriented, sporty style, with GT-tuned suspension and steering, sports seating, and a standard PHEV powertrain with AWD.
2027 Toyota RAV4 PHEV GR-Sport interior (Source: Toyota)
Inside, the 2027 RAV4 includes a standard 12.3″ digital cluster and a 10.5″ touchscreen with the Toyota Audio Multimedia system, plus wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
A 12.9″ touchscreen with a JBL Premium Audio system with 9 speakers is standard on the Limited trim and available on the XSE grade.

title: Electric cars are about to overtake petrol in the UK, data shows
content:
Battery-electric cars took 32% of the UK’s new car market in October, while petrol cars fell to just 37.2%, according to new data from the SMMT. That’s the closest the two have been.
At the current pace, electric cars will outsell petrol in the UK within a year. And it could happen as soon as this December.
October: EVs up 33%, petrol down 12%
The UK registered 152,730 new cars in October, up 5.4% year-over-year and the 11th straight month of growth for the overall market.
All of that growth came from plug-ins. BEV registrations jumped 32.7% to 48,858 units, and plug-in hybrids rose 30.1% to 22,898. Meanwhile, petrol fell 11.6% to 56,876 units, diesel dropped 15.9%, and even conventional hybrids were down 5%.
Through the first 10 months of the year, the UK has now registered 503,805 BEVs, up 30.4%, for a 26.6% market share. Petrol’s year-to-date share is down to 41.1%, from 47.2% at the same point last year.
The trend points to 2027, or sooner
We pulled SMMT’s monthly fuel-type data going back to March 2024 to see where this is heading. Note that SMMT counts mild hybrids as petrol (or diesel) in its headline categories, and that’s generally how we count them at Electrek.
In March 2024, petrol held 55.9% of the market and BEVs 15.2%. In October 2026, it was 37.2% vs 32.0%. Petrol’s share is shrinking by about half a point per month on a linear trend, while BEVs gain about 0.36 points a month. Extend both lines and they cross around August 2027 at roughly 33% each.
But that’s the slow scenario, because it ignores December.
UK BEV share spikes every December as automakers push volume to get closer to their ZEV Mandate targets. BEVs hit 31.0% in December 2024 and 32.2% in December 2025, when petrol was at 39.4%. Over the last five months, BEV share has run about 5 points higher than a year earlier, and petrol about 7 points lower. If December follows that pattern, BEVs land around 37% and petrol around 32%.
That would be the first time BEVs beat petrol in SMMT’s headline numbers, mild hybrids included.
However, SMMT’s own forecast of 27.2% BEV share for the full year implies roughly 31% for November and December combined, which would make it a much closer call. And on a stricter definition that puts mild hybrids with hybrids instead of petrol, BEVs already outsold every other powertrain in August.
Zoom out to full years and the picture is just as clear. Cars that run only on petrol or diesel, mild hybrids included, made up 72.5% of the UK market in 2021. This year, they’re at 45.5%.
Automakers still want the mandate cut
None of this is good enough for the SMMT, which is using the release to push the government, again, to cut the ZEV Mandate targets.
The mandate requires 33% of 2026 sales to be zero-emission. SMMT now forecasts 27.2%. It expects 32% next year against a 38% target, and 37.5% in 2028 against 52%, a 14.5-point gap.
The trade group says automakers have spent “billions” on discounts, 0% financing, deposit contributions, and even subsidized charging to move EVs, on top of the government’s Electric Car Grant. It also slammed last week’s Budget, which confirmed a new EV-specific road tax (eVED) starting in 2028 and kept 20% VAT on public charging.
“Higher targets may force supply, but they do not create demand,” SMMT chief executive Mike Hawes said.
We’ve heard this one before. The SMMT made the same argument after September’s record 99,199 BEV registrations, and the government already opened a review of the mandate this year.
Chinese brands are taking the growth
This might be the main reason why the trade group wants to slow things down. The brands growing fastest in the UK are mostly Chinese. BYD registered 6,065 cars in October, up 73%. Jaecoo more than doubled to 6,089 units, Chery nearly tripled to 3,707, and Leapmotor doubled to 1,773. MG was up 85%.
Tesla, on the other hand, registered just 282 cars in October, down 45% from 511 a year ago. The first month of the quarter is always slow for Tesla in the UK, and the brand is still up 31% year-to-date at 46,526 units after a big September. But it didn’t have a single model in October’s top 10 BEVs, which was led by the Skoda Enyaq (1,568), Mini Countryman (1,494), and Jaecoo 5 (1,465).
Electrek’s Take
The SMMT’s framing is that there’s a “demand gap.” The data shows the opposite. BEV registrations are up 30% this year while petrol is shrinking every single month. That’s not a market rejecting EVs.
Top comment by European Bob
The SMMT is not a neutral organisation, they have been briefing against EVs for years and continue to do so.
The ZEV mandate is NOT a measure of how many pure BEVs are sold, and the SMMT know it, it's a measure of REDUCING emission against a level set in the past.
Those emissions reductions can be met by selling BEVs, or selling more efficient PHEVs or even selling more efficient petrol or diesel cars! The manufacturers can also buy credits if they choose to.
NO manufacturer has paid any ZEV fines to date (DfT announcement March 2026)
As for the "heavy discounts" and "loss making sales", well I have two data points on that.
1. The retail price of EVs has continued to climb in the UK over the past 6 years, despite the cost of any average 50kWh battery pack dropping several thousand dollars.
2. There are hundreds of main dealerships who are buying cars from the manufacturers, driving them for the minimum 3 month period, often with just a few thousand miles on the clock and then selling them with a 30-35% retail price discount, and then repeating ad infinitum. The dealerships are still making a few thousand with each transaction, so we know where the manufacturers price really sits.
And the discounts automakers keep complaining about? That’s the mandate doing exactly what it was designed to do. It forces automakers to sell EVs, so they price them to sell, and buyers respond. Hawes says targets don’t create demand, but cheaper EVs clearly do. October proves it.
Now, is the jump to 52% in 2028 steep? It is steep, but it looks achievable to me. If anything is hurting demand, it’s the government’s own moves: a new EV-only road tax and 20% VAT on public charging. That’s what the industry should be fighting. It’s too early for that.
Either way, petrol’s days as the UK’s default car are numbered. The only question is whether the milestone comes in December or sometime in 2027. Our bet is December.

title: DeepWay electric semi arrives in New Zealand, and gets a new name
content:
Electric Semi Truck
New Zealand
Jo Borrás
| Nov 5 2026 - 4:10 am PT
New Zealand’s Foodstuffs North Island Limited has given its latest electric semi truck an electrifying new identity, courtesy of a second-grade student at a local elementary school.
The Chinese-built DeepWay Star began delivering chilled and frozen groceries across New Zealand’s lower North Island earlier this year
– and, after a naming competition organized with students at Russell Street School in Palmerston North, the big HD EV has got a new name:
The winning name came from Year 2 (read: second grade) student named Madison, who beat out suggestions including Buzzy Bee, Lightning, and Bolt. Madison got to officially unveil the truck’s new name alongside her classmates, local officials and Foodstuffs representatives.
“Our trucks are out on the road every day delivering food to stores and communities, so we thought it would be great to get the kids involved and give our first electric truck a bit of personality,” explains Foodstuffs North Island General Manager Supply Chain, Yang Zhang. “There were some brilliant ideas, but Evie was a pretty fitting name for an EV. The best part is knowing Madison and the other students will be able to spot Evie out on the road and know they played a part in it.”
Looking forward
Madison was allowed to do the unveiling honors, revealing Evie’s new name alongside her other classmates, Palmerston North’s Mayor, Grant Smith, local MP Tangi Utikeri, and local PAK’nSAVE, New World, and Four Square grocers who will be receiving deliveries from Evie.
In its first few months on the road, Evie’s travelled nearly 45,000 kilometers (~28,000 miles) and avoided more than 81,000 kg of harmful carbon emissions –
which the company claims is roughly equivalent to taking 35 ICE cars off the road for a full year
As for the truck itself, it has a sort of Tesla-ish, anteater-y look, and significantly longer range than the StarWay, offering more than 500 km (~310 miles)
of range from its 600 kWh CATL-built LFP battery packs that can plug into charge ports two at a time for lickety-quick charging in about 30 minutes
. If that’s too long of a wait,
the Star can swap its tired batteries for fresh ones in special battery-sway stations in just six minutes
The DeepWay’s electric motors put out 491 kW (~660 hp) of power, and a positively tectonic 75,000 (!) Nm (~55,000 lb-ft) (!!) of torque – more than enough to get the 50 tons (100,000 lb.) of GVWR it’s rated for up to speed.
You can check out the pictures, above, then let us know what you think of the big Chinese BEV and it’s fun new name in the comments.

title: Aniioki A9 Pro Max review: Basically an electric motorcycle that you can pedal
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Electric Mopeds
Micah Toll
| Nov 5 2026 - 3:25 am PT
There are electric bikes, there are electric motorcycles, and then there are machines like the Aniioki
A9 Pro Max
that plant a flag somewhere in the increasingly large no-man’s-land between the two.
Technically, it has pedals. You can pedal it fairly effectively too, with the actually adjustable seat. You can even pedal it for fun, which is more than I can say for some of the increasingly motorcycle-shaped “e-bikes” I’ve tested lately.
But let’s get something out of the way right at the beginning:
this isn’t a street-legal electric bicycle in the US
. Not when we’re talking about dual motors producing up to 6,000W of peak power and speeds of around 45 mph.
And you know what? That’s fine. As long as we’re all honest about what this thing is.
A whole lot of bike
The Aniioki A9 Pro Max is absolutely massive, and the spec sheet makes that abundantly clear.
The version I tested uses a pair of 2,500W direct-drive hub motors, one in each wheel, with Aniioki claiming 3,000W peak power from each motor. That gives the bike a combined peak figure of 6,000W and up to 250 Nm of combined torque. It’s hard to overstate how massive that is.
Then there’s the battery. You can choose between a 60V 70Ah pack with 4.2 kWh of capacity or an even larger 60V 80Ah pack packing 4.8 kWh. For comparison, many typical commuter e-bikes have somewhere around 500-700 Wh of battery. The smaller battery here is roughly six to eight times that size. That’s absolutely in the territory of
legit light electric motorcycles.
Aniioki claims up to 230+ miles (370 km) of pedal-assist range, though as usual, you should take maximum e-bike range figures as best-case numbers. Using the throttle and enjoying those big motors is going to dramatically reduce that figure. Even so, with more than 4 kWh of battery underneath you, range anxiety isn’t exactly the first thing that comes to mind.
All that hardware comes with a predictable penalty: weight. The 70Ah model tips the scales at around 188 lb (85 kg), while the 80Ah version approaches 193 lb (87.5 kg). Those aren’t e-bike weights. Those are motorcycle weights. Again, you can see the direction this is going.
But surprisingly, you can actually pedal it
Here’s where the A9 Pro Max gets more interesting to me.
A lot of high-powered e-motos include pedals seemingly as a regulatory fig leaf. They’re technically there, but the geometry is so bad that nobody in their right mind would want to pedal the thing farther than across a parking lot. Even some smaller and presumably Class 2 legal e-bikes that have moto-style frames are nearly unpedalable for actual riding over any reasonable distance.
But the A9 here is actually pedalable thanks to having something that more closely resembles a bicycle seat, plus adjustability that lets riders dial in the correct seat height.
The A9 Pro Max feels more like a strange combination of an oversized fat-tire e-bike and a small electric motorcycle. There’s a Shimano 7-speed drivetrain and a huge 72-tooth chainring, meaning the pedals aren’t entirely ornamental.
I actually enjoyed pedaling it with the pedal assist engaged. You’re obviously not going to mistake a nearly 200-pound machine rolling on enormous 26 x 4.8-inch tires for a lightweight fitness bike, but there’s something fun about contributing some human power while two giant hub motors do most of the heavy lifting.
And when you don’t feel like pedaling, there’s a full-twist throttle waiting for you.
That combination is really the appeal here. You can ride it more like an e-bike when the mood strikes, or twist the throttle and treat it more like a lightweight e-moto.
And again, I don’t want to beat a dead horse here, but remember: the pedals don’t make this an electric bicycle. It’s still an e-moto, but it’s one that you can actually have fun pedaling. You can treat it like a mech suit, where pedaling translates into crazy power, as if you have super-human legs. And with the insanely large 72t chainring, pedaling at higher speeds is actually doable. Though I’ll tell you right now, pedaling at 40 mph (64 km/h) is not exactly a normal or natural feeling.
And it’s worth pointing out that at a starting price of
US $2,899
(or more for the larger battery capacities), that’s a fairly reasonable price compared to most e-motos that can be more limiting in how and where you can ride them.
Motorcycle performance deserves motorcycle hardware
Fortunately, Aniioki seems to understand that putting this much power on two wheels requires more serious components than the average bicycle.
The braking setup is particularly wild. There are two massive 300mm brake rotors on the front wheel and another 300mm rotor out back, along with a linked CBS braking system. The front uses custom eight-piston calipers (the pair of quad-piston calipers) while the rear gets a custom six-piston setup.
There’s also an adjustable air-suspension fork with 110mm of travel, rear suspension to smooth out bumps at higher speeds, integrated lighting and turn signals, and a large five-inch display that even incorporates features like Bluetooth audio and a recording camera.
Know where you can ride it
That brings us to the elephant in the room.
In the US, consumer-product rules generally define a low-speed electric bicycle around a motor of less than 750W and a maximum motor-powered speed below 20 mph (32 km/h), while individual states use their own operating laws that typically match the familiar Class 1/2/3 framework. A 6,000W machine capable of around 45 mph (72 km/h) blows straight through normal limits.
So please don’t see pedals and assume this belongs on your local bicycle path.
Where and how you can legally operate something like the A9 Pro Max depends on your local laws and whether it can qualify under another vehicle category. For many owners, the sensible place to enjoy its full performance is going to be private property or other areas where such vehicles are permitted.
That caveat doesn’t make the bike itself bad. It just means buyers need to understand what they’re buying.
And judged on what it actually is rather than what the word “e-bike” on the product page suggests, I had a lot of fun on it.
There are certainly riders who would look at a nearly 200-pound, 45 mph machine and say, “Why not just buy an electric motorcycle?” That’s a perfectly reasonable question.
But I also understand the appeal of this weird middle ground. The A9 Pro Max retains enough bicycle DNA that you can pedal it around and enjoy pedal assist, yet has enough battery and motor underneath you to deliver something much closer to small-motorcycle performance when you twist the throttle.
Imagine going off-road and getting to fly up hills while pedaling hard, but then being able to switch to throttle once your legs get worn out. Sure, it’s not everyone’s cup of tea, but it’s a cup of tea.
This bike is big. It’s heavy. It’s absurdly powerful by e-bike standards. And it absolutely isn’t the machine I’d recommend for someone looking for a normal street-legal electric bicycle.
But if what you actually want is a big, powerful electric two-wheeler that still lets you turn the pedals when the mood strikes, the Aniioki A9 Pro Max makes a surprisingly compelling argument for this increasingly bizarre category of pedal-equipped e-motos.

title: Congo launches energy supply study into economic zones, industries - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
The study plans to establish a pricing benchmark for the Congolese industrial market after the country’s industrial development minister referred to current solar electricity price offers as low as XAF 130 ($0.22)/kWh as ‘opportunistic’.
Patrick Jowett
05 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Research & Development
Commercial & industrial
Highlights
The Republic of the Congo is working on a study examining electricity supply needs for its special economic zones (SEZs) and industrial facilities.
The initiative, which aims to assess suitable supply solutions as the country’s electricity demand increases, was launched earlier this week by Michel Djombo, the country’s Minister of Industrial Development, SEZs and Private Sector Promotion.
It will be conducted under supervision of the Ministry of Energy and Hydraulics, implemented by the National Agency for Rural Electrification and supported technically by the United Nations Development Programme.
The study will compare four potential approaches to meeting industrial electricity demand: solar paired with battery storage, biomass and cogeneration using agricultural, forestry and agro-industrial residues, connections to the national grid where available, and hybrid energy systems.
It is also expected to establish a pricing benchmark for energy solutions in the Congolese industrial market.
Speaking at a launch event, Djombo questioned solar electricity offers priced at between XAF 130 ($0.22) and XAF 150/kWh, describing some as opportunistic, and said international comparisons would help establish fair and sustainable pricing.
The minister also highlighted the cost of relying on diesel generators during periods of electricity supply disruption, saying the price of generated electricity can reach almost XAF 200/kWh.
Electricity supply constraints are impacting industrial operators in the country, the minister continued, with some companies reportedly having to suspend production lines. Despite high diesel prices, Djomobo also revealed some industrial operators remain reluctant to commit to alternative energy solutions and are waiting for market conditions to become clearer.
The initiative plans to also examine different commercial arrangements for supplying industrial customers, including turnkey installations financed directly by businesses, financing services for equipment purchases and introducing independent power producers. It is also expected to identify bankable projects capable of attracting public and private investment.
The Africa Solar Industry Association (AFSIA) has identified 35.6 MW of operational solar in the Republic of the Congo to date, according to figures available in its project database, 27 MW of which is listed as unidentified C&I projects.

title: China’s energy storage fleet grows to 167 GW as utilization improves - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
The NEA reported 63% annual growth in installed capacity, alongside longer storage durations and improving utilization rates.
Vincent Shaw
05 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Batteries
Energy Storage
Highlights
A shift in China’s energy policy has dramatically changed the revenue model for battery storage, opening up revenue opportunities from capacity payments, arbitrage, and ancillary services.
China’s operational new-type energy storage capacity reached 167 GW/435 GWh at the end of September 2026, up 63% year on year, according to figures released by the National Energy Administration (NEA) on October 30.
The data were presented at the agency’s quarterly press conference on national energy developments. China’s new-type energy storage category covers electrochemical, compressed-air and other emerging storage systems, but excludes conventional pumped hydro.
Compared with 135.93 GW/351.12 GWh at the end of 2025, the latest figures indicate a net capacity increase of approximately 31 GW/84 GWh during the first nine months of 2026.
The NEA reported that average storage duration had increased to 2.61 hours, up approximately 0.27 hours year on year. Equivalent utilization hours reached around 915 hours during the nine-month period, an increase of approximately 10 hours compared with the same period of 2025.
The improvements suggest that China’s storage expansion is being accompanied by gradual changes in system configuration and utilization, rather than growth in installed capacity alone.
According to the NEA, the rapid development of new-type storage has been supported by government policies, technological innovation, industrial supply chains and growing demand for flexibility in the power system.
China’s combined wind and solar generating capacity exceeded 2.01 TW at the end of September, accounting for approximately 48.7% of total installed power capacity. As variable renewable generation expands, storage is increasingly needed to absorb surplus electricity, shift generation to higher-demand periods and provide fast-response grid services.
The structure of China’s storage market is also changing. Official figures for 2025 showed that independent energy storage facilities accounted for 51.2% of cumulative new-type storage installations. Projects rated at 100 MW or above represented 72% of installed capacity, while systems with durations of at least four hours accounted for 27.6%.
Lithium-ion batteries remained the dominant technology, representing approximately 96% of installed new-type storage capacity, although compressed-air, flow batteries and other technologies are gradually expanding their presence.
Market reforms are expected to reinforce these trends. China has been developing arrangements allowing independent storage operators to earn revenues from electricity trading, ancillary services and capacity remuneration, gradually reducing reliance on mandatory storage requirements associated with renewable projects.
Under the country’s 15th Five-Year Plan for power system development, new-type energy storage capacity is targeted to reach 300 GW by 2030, with greater emphasis on longer-duration systems, grid-forming capabilities and improved operational efficiency.
The growing contribution of storage is already visible in renewable-rich regional grids. In western Inner Mongolia, the grid operator reported 20.23 GW/70.47 GWh of operational storage capacity in October. During emergency dispatch operations, storage supplied up to 12.25 GW, equivalent to 33% of the grid’s electricity demand at the time.
Such examples illustrate how storage can provide substantial short-term balancing capacity in electricity systems with high renewable penetration. For other countries expanding wind and solar generation, China’s deployment offers experience in large-scale storage manufacturing, grid integration and centralized dispatch.

content:
Markets & Policy
Malawi officially launched its net-metering framework, allowing eligible consumers to export surplus solar electricity to the grid in exchange for credits. Pilot implementation is underway, targeting 34 prosumers with approximately 3.9 MW of capacity, while nationwide rollout remains unconfirmed.
Emiliano Bellini
05 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Highlights
Malawi’s Ministry of Energy and the Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (MERA) have launched a net metering scheme intended at supporting residential PV deployment across the country.
“The new regulatory frameworks would enable households and businesses to generate their own electricity and supply surplus power to the national grid, reducing reliance on conventional energy sources and promoting a cleaner, more affordable and sustainable energy future for Malawi,” said Minister of Energy, Jean Mathanga.
Implementation activities had already commenced in May 2026 under the Electricity Supply Corporation of Malawi (ESCOM). An initial pilot programme is expected to involve 34 eligible prosumers, with a combined generation capacity of approximately 3.9 MW. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has also demonstrated the practical application of net metering through a solar PV installation connected to the national grid.
Although the regulatory framework has been introduced and pilot implementation is underway, the extent of nationwide commercial deployment remains unclear. In particular, the availability of the scheme to all eligible customers, applicable compensation arrangements and detailed administrative procedures require further verification.
Malawi’s electricity sector has historically faced challenges related to grid instability, dependence on hydropower, renewable energy curtailment and reliance on costly diesel backup generation. To address these challenges and facilitate greater integration of renewable energy, the country has recently invested in grid-scale energy storage infrastructure.
In July 2026, Malawi inaugurated its first utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS), located in Kanengo, Lilongwe. The facility has a capacity of 20 MW/40 MWh and was developed by ESCOM with support from the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (GEAPP), including $20 million in grant financing.
According to the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), the country had 105 MW of installed PV capacity at the end of 2025.

title: Hoymiles plans to establish inverter factory in Oman - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Chinese inverter manufacturer Hoymiles has signed a strategic agreement with three partners to develop solar, energy storage and manufacturing projects in Oman. The proposed $100 million partnership includes a renewable energy investment fund and a solar inverter manufacturing facility targeting Middle Eastern and North African markets.
Vincent Shaw
05 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Asia-Pacific
Inverters
Hoymiles’ HMS-2000 micro-inverter
Chinese solar inverter manufacturer
Hoymiles
has signed a four-party strategic cooperation agreement with PCG Global, the Oman Investment Authority (OIA), and Greenwill Asset Management to explore renewable energy investment, project development, and local manufacturing in Oman.
The agreement was signed in Beijing on Nov. 2, during Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tarik’s state visit to China. The signing ceremony was attended by the sultan and Mu Hong, vice chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference.
The partners plan to establish the Oman New Energy Ecosystem Cooperation Fund, targeting distributed solar and energy storage projects, integrated power supply solutions for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, and investments in renewable energy-related industries.
Hoymiles said the fund will primarily invest in renewable power generation assets in Oman, supporting local project development and operations.
In a separate announcement, OIA said it had signed a preliminary term sheet with Hoymiles and PCG Global for a proposed partnership valued at OMR 38.45 million ($100 million). The agreement covers solar project development and a solar inverter manufacturing facility serving markets across the Middle East and North Africa.
OIA, Oman’s sovereign wealth fund, is expected to act as an anchor investor in the proposed fund and coordinate with local authorities and project partners. It did not clarify whether the $100 million represents the proposed fund’s capitalization or a broader investment commitment.
Singapore-based PCG Global will focus on project development, construction, and operations, drawing on the experience of Chinese distributed energy developer PCG Power. Its planned activities include commercial and industrial solar projects, off-grid power systems, and integrated energy solutions for AI data centers.
Hong Kong-based Greenwill Asset Management will oversee fund management and investment activities.
PCG Global was established by the team behind PCG Power. In July 2026, it secured pre-Series A funding led by GenZero, an investment platform owned by Singapore’s Temasek, to support its international renewable energy expansion.
The agreement comes as Oman seeks to diversify its economy and expand renewable power generation. The country aims to generate approximately 30% of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030.
A China-Oman joint statement issued on Nov. 2 also called for closer cooperation in solar and wind power, electricity transmission and conversion, energy storage, and AI.

title: Revolta installs first 10 kWh sodium-ion home battery in Germany - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
The German startup has commissioned its first customer system in an unusual place, with further pilot installations planned across Germany in the coming weeks.
Tristan Rayner
05 Nov 2026
Applications & Installations
Batteries
Energy Storage
Residential
Frankfurt-based Revolta has installed and commissioned its first sodium-ion home battery at a customer property near Aschaffenburg, Germany.
The high-voltage system, oeprating at a nominal voltage of 450 V, comprises five battery modules with a combined capacity of 10 kWh. While not setting any records for installation size, the sodium-ion storage system rollout continues and provides both Revolta and the industry a look at customer site usage, with operating data to follow.
The property already has around 20 kW of solar PV and a small hydroelectric plant housed in a former mill. The hydro plant has supplied the family with electricity since 2017.
According to Revolta, the owner had been waiting specifically for a suitable sodium-ion home battery, with greater energy independence given as the motivation. Revolta team members Julian Mattheis and Florina Thaler carried out the installation and commissioning.
Each 2 kWh battery module weighs 18.7 kg and has IP64 protection according to the data sheet, with the installation using an SMA inverter. Each module uses only three battery cells, and batteries are charged and discharged at 0.4 C (or 2.5 hour power duration). In this 10 kWh configuration, a maxium 4 kW power output could be expected.
Energy density is published at 141 Wh/l, 107 Wh/kg.
Further installations at selected customer sites across Germany are planned over the coming weeks. Revolta is supplying pilot customers with an additional measuring device at no charge to collect data on how the systems perform in daily operation. The findings will feed into development of its battery management system and firmware.
The company describes the installation as the start of its commercial launch, although the rollout remains at the pilot stage. Its announcement did not disclose pricing, rated power, cycle life or efficiency figures.
Revolta notes it is sold out for 2026, but offers a resevation for 2027. It publishes a list price of €599 ($672.5) per 2 kWh module, and lists a price for give modules for the 10 kWh installation at €2,995.

title: Pairing residential heat pumps with potassium carbonate-based thermochemical storage - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
U.S. researchers have found that combining residential heat pumps with thermochemical energy storage could reduce electricity demand during cold spells. Improved storage efficiency and heat pump performance could increase the contribution of thermal storage in highly decarbonized power grids.
Lior Kahana
05 Nov 2026
Research & Development
Heat pumps
Residential
Illustration of the system
A research team at
Pennsylvania State University
in the USA evaluated residential heat pumps paired with thermochemical energy storage (TCES) for long-duration energy storage. The researchers aimed to determine whether storing heat ahead of cold spells could reduce heating-related electricity demand when heat pumps become less efficient and the grid faces greater pressure.
“In this paper, we model a TCES system using potassium carbonate (K₂CO₃) as the thermochemical material (TCM),” the group explained. “This system can be thermally charged by an electric heat pump well in advance and discharged to meet the building’s heating load during the heating season. The optimal operation is assessed during the most stressful time of the heating season, based on projections for 2050.”
The researchers used simulation and linear optimization to evaluate an air-source heat pump coupled with potassium carbonate-based TCES and a battery in a 220.82 m² single-family home under New York City conditions. Hourly grid projections for a 95% decarbonized electricity system in 2050 were translated into a varying building electricity-demand limit.
The TCES model represented heat storage through salt dehydration and heat release through hydration, with approximately 80 C water required for charging and 35 C water supplied to radiant heating during discharge. The team further optimized hourly operation to minimize electricity consumption while meeting heating demand and respecting the electricity limit.
Reference charging/discharging efficiencies were 45%/80% for TCES and 95%/95% for the battery. Across 96 simulations, they varied heat-pump performance, TCES specific heating power, and charging efficiency to assess their effects on required storage capacities.
According to the results, the reference system required 68 kWh of thermal storage and 168 kWh of battery capacity, with batteries providing most of the storage response. Higher warm-weather heat-pump coefficient of performance (COP), improved TCES charging efficiency, and greater specific heating power favored thermal storage, while better cold-weather COP reduced both storage requirements. In the scenario most favorable to thermal storage, the optimized TCES capacity requirement was 894 kWh.
“These findings suggest two potential pathways for future researchers and manufacturers to enable efficient, long-duration energy storage responses from heat pumps and TCES systems,” the academics noted. “The first approach involves increasing TCES’s charge efficiency from 45% to 65%, while the second involves enhancing the heat pump’s COP by at least 25%, even if it degrades in cold climates.”
The researchers said further development of the proposed configuration could focus on enhancing the thermal storage system’s specific heating power. Such advances could enable TCES to provide a greater share of heating demand during periods of grid stress, reducing reliance on battery storage. However, the viability of the combined system would depend on improvements in component performance and the ability to integrate thermal storage with residential heating systems.

title: What Class A reveals about solar PV module fire performance - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
When it comes to solar PV module safety, it’s important to understand how Class A designations differ. Any Class A claim must identify the standard used.
05 Nov 2026
Technology & Products
solar modules
While two solar modules can carry the same Class A designation, they can differ in their fire performance. The shared label can conceal differences that matter for the safety of the building below.
Class A is a defined classification reached through prescribed test criteria, and any Class A claim must identify the standard used. It should not automatically be interpreted as “fireproof”, nor does the classification itself tell a potential user how far beyond the pass threshold a particular solar module performed.
The first distinction is what the test measures: resistance to an external fire or the product’s contribution to fire development.
Under UL 790, Class A describes performance under severe external fire exposure. It does not classify the module’s materials as non-combustible.
European standards assess a product’s contribution to fire development under EN 13501-1 and a roof’s response to external fire under EN 13501-5. UL 790 Class A does not establish compliance with either; each requires separate evidence.
Even under UL 790, flames can spread farther across one module than another and both still pass Class A. Buyers need measured test results to compare them. A “pass” alone does not show how close either came to the limit.
Fire-resistant glass is only part of the design
A claim about fire-resistant glass says little about how the complete solar PV module behaves. The encapsulation beneath it can contribute to fire development, so flame-retardant materials also have a role in limiting fire propagation. Electrical faults create ignition risks that the glass does not prevent.
Cell-level current management can limit hot spots under shading, and reinforced electrical connections can reduce fault and arcing risks. A complete assessment of module fire safety must therefore examine both its response to external fire and the design features that reduce the risk of a fire starting within it.
LONGi’s Hi-MO X10 Guardian Fire-Resistant solar module incorporates these features alongside fire-resistant glass. The module passed TÜV Rheinland’s UL 790 Class A spread-of-flame and burning-brand tests. The burning source did not penetrate the module or roof covering, and the module did not sustain flaming. The test specimens were randomly selected from a normal production batch.
The Hi-MO X10 Guardian Fire-Resistant module also achieved Class B under EN 13501-1 for reaction to fire and passed testing for B ROOF (t4) under EN 13501-5 – the highest external roof-fire performance classification within the t4 method.

title: Korean researchers build all-solid battery prototype with 235.13 Wh/L energy density - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Researchers at South Korea’s Dongguk University have developed an anode-free all-solid-state thin-film battery featuring an ultrathin tin/carbon interlayer to improve lithium deposition and cycling stability. The 2.77-micrometer-thick prototype achieved a volumetric energy density of 235.13 Wh/L after 100 cycles, potentially paving the way for more reliable solid-state batteries.
Emiliano Bellini
05 Nov 2026
Research & Development
Batteries
Energy Storage
Solid-state batteries (SSBs) remain far from mainstream adoption in battery energy storage systems (BESS), as their potential benefits have yet to outweigh high costs, manufacturing challenges and limited commercial experience. Although they promise improved safety, higher energy density and potentially longer lifetimes, grid-scale storage has different priorities from electric vehicles. For BESS applications, affordability, cycle life, reliability, safety and bankability are more important than energy density, making established lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries difficult to displace.
SSBs also also face challenges related to uneven lithium plating and stripping during operation, which can cause interfacial instability, void formation and lithium (Li) filament growth. These effects can accelerate degradation, increase the risk of internal short circuits and compromise the long-term reliability required for stationary energy storage applications.
To address this challenge, researchers at South Korea’s Dongguk University have developed an anode-free all-solid-state battery (ASSB) in which Li from the cathode is deposited directly onto a bare current collector during the initial charging cycle, forming an anode in situ. “This architecture enhances volumetric energy density and simplifies fabrication, particularly for thin-film batteries. However, it is vulnerable to Li loss caused by uneven deposition, electrically isolated ‘dead’ lithium, or loss of contact with the solid electrolyte during stripping, compromising battery stability and capacity,” they explained.
The proposed innovation relies on what the research group describes as an anode-less thin-film battery platform using an ultrathin tin/carbon (Sn/C) interlayer, which is intended to eliminate the need for a conventional lithium-metal anode during manufacturing. Instead, a very thin coating of tin and carbon is applied to the anode-side current collector to control how lithium deposits during charging.
“Our interlayer acts as a seed for Li nucleation, promoting uniform Li plating and reducing Li loss and improving the reversibility of repeated charging and discharging,” said lead author Hyun-Suk Kim.
The battery prototype features a modified copper current collector coated with ultrathin layers of tin and carbon, an architecture the researchers identified as the most effective after evaluating several metal-based, carbon-based and hybrid coatings. Their experiments showed that the Sn/C combination offered superior control over Li deposition while improving stability at the electrode interface.
The improvement stems from the different functions of the two materials. Tin provides favorable sites for lithium to accumulate by lowering the energy required to initiate deposition, while carbon helps distribute the deposited lithium more evenly. This combination limits irregular growth and supports a more stable interface during repeated charging and discharging.
To further improve performance, the team added a small amount of metallic Li to the coated current collector before cycling. This “prelithiation” step creates a lithium reserve intended to compensate for irreversible losses during early operation, addressing a key limitation of anode-free battery designs.
The researchers assembled the modified current collector (Cu@Sn/C) with a lithium vanadium oxide (LVO) cathode and a lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) solid electrolyte. The resulting cell, measuring only 2.77 micrometers thick, delivered a volumetric energy density of 235.13 Wh/L at the 100th cycle, under a reported cycling rate of 0.01 C.
Microscopic analysis also provided insight into the battery’s stability. During the first lithium deposition, a three-dimensional structure containing tin and lithium–tin alloy developed within the interlayer. This structure helped accommodate the physical changes associated with subsequent cycling, reducing disruption at the interface and supporting more consistent battery operation.
“Our approach shows how interface engineering and lithium-inventory management can improve anode-less thin-film batteries,” said Kim. “This approach could support the development of ultrathin batteries for wearable electronics, IoT sensors, and medical devices, as well as scalable anode-less ASSBs for industrial-scale power.”
The novel SSB concept was presented in “
Pushing Energy Density Limits: Anode-Less Solid-State Battery Integrated With Amorphous Lithium Vanadium Oxide Thin-Film Cathode
,” published in
Advanced Energy Materials

title: Quantum computers pose imminent threat to digital locks at banks
content: RSA-2048, the high-end encryption protecting your bank accounts and data online, can be cracked with a quantum computer with 23,000 qubits. This was discovered by the French firm Alice & Bob after a detailed study. While this is an estimate, the quantum computing firm believes this could become a reality by the end of the decade. RSA-2048 is the gold standard of encryption. It secures our digital infrastructure, from websites and social media to online banking and data storage. It is considered incredibly difficult to break because it requires factoring a 617-digit modulus into two prime numbers. In practice, the encryption is easy to create but difficult to crack. This is because classical computers would spend astronomical amounts of money to solve the encryption, which would dwarf the gains made by breaking the encryption. With a quantum computer, though, the situation changes completely, and breaking the encryption can be relatively easy and cost-effective. What is Shor’s algorithm? In 1994, mathematician Peter Shor gave the world his famous algorithm that could crack the RSA-2048 encryption. The only hurdle is that this algorithm needs a quantum computer that is large enough and accurate enough to run it.Since physical qubits are error-prone, the quantum computer running Shor’s algorithm will also need an error-correction mechanism to ensure it gives the right answers. In 2019, Google Quantum AI researchers predicted that a quantum computer with 20 million physical qubits would be needed to break RSA-2048. Over the next six years, this number fell to below one million. This improvement is partly due to increased efficiency that mathematicians have brought to the algorithm itself over 30 years of its existence. The other is due to advances in quantum computing technologies that have led to better logical performance from qubits. Where cat qubits can helpA French quantum computing firm that uses cat qubits made a similar estimate for Shor’s algorithm in 2023 and found it would need only 350,000 qubits to crack it. A more updated estimate using improved cat qubits now puts this number at 23,000 and the time needed to crack the encryption at 3.14 days. While 23,000 qubits isn’t something that a quantum computer is capable of today, the number is relatively low to be reachable in the next few years. Along with the qubits, the run time is also important. So, a quantum computer with 610,530 cat qubits could do the same job in just 1.5 hours. The challenge of scaling to this many qubits is the additional infrastructure required to run such a quantum computer and still fit it all in a decently sized laboratory. Researchers at Alice & Bob reckon that building such a quantum computer will be possible in just a few years from now and RSA-2048 encryption would be rendered obsolete. Luckily, there are post-quantum encryption standards that already exist but have not been extensively tested. The paper encourages the cybersecurity community to test these more rigorously and transition systems to these new algorithms before quantum computers become more common. The research is not peer-reviewed and is published in the Cryptology ePrint Archive.

title: China starts 660 MW unit at highest-altitude coal power project
content: A 660-megawatt coal-fired unit began commercial operations Thursday in Golmud, in China’s northwestern Qinghai Province, after completing a 168-hour trial run, state broadcaster CCTV News reported. It is the first of two units at China’s highest-altitude ultra-supercritical coal power project, which sits at an average elevation of about 9,350 feet (2,850 meters).The project is designed to help stabilize Qinghai’s power grid by adjusting its output as renewable generation fluctuates. Bringing the first unit online meant tackling two problems inside the boiler. Thin air makes it harder to burn coal efficiently, and the fuel’s high alkali content can cause slag and ash to build up.Burning coal in thin airLower atmospheric pressure at the site reduces the amount of oxygen available for combustion. The project uses oxygen-assisted startup to help get the boiler firing and separate combustion controls to keep it running steadily when the unit is operating at very low output.Engineers also customized the boiler to handle high-alkali coal, which can leave deposits inside the system. Together, the changes allow the unit to burn the fuel while varying its output to match demand on the grid, according to CCTV News.The unit uses ultra-supercritical technology, which typically operates with steam above 1,076°F (580°C) and at pressures above 24 megapascals. Those conditions allow a plant to generate more electricity from the same amount of coal. CCTV News reported that the project uses less coal per unit of electricity supplied than China’s national benchmark.Giving renewables flexible backupThe ability to keep the boiler running at very low output gives the grid more flexibility when renewable generation is strong. The coal unit can cut its output during those periods and increase it when renewable generation falls, or the grid needs more power.Zhao Falin, the project’s chief manager at Huadian Golmud Co., said the two units are expected to generate 6 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity annually once both are operating. That would be enough to meet the yearly electricity needs of about 6.6 million residents, he said.Zhao added that the project would improve the stability and reliability of Qinghai’s grid by providing backup capacity as more renewable power comes online.Recycling water for the second unitThe plant treats and reuses reclaimed municipal wastewater from Golmud. The water circulates through a closed-loop system that, according to the report, allows the plant to operate with zero wastewater discharge. The project also reported that it puts 100 percent of its solid waste to use.CCTV News reported that preparations are underway for the second 660-megawatt unit’s full-system startup. The project aims to have both units in commercial service by the end of the year, bringing its combined generating capacity to 1,320 megawatts.The second unit will add as much generating capacity as the first. Once both are running, the project will also provide flexible backup as Qinghai brings more renewable generation online.

title: US ally tests 49-foot rocket to develop next-gen hypersonic weapons
content: France has successfully launched its SyLEx sounding rocket for the second time, marking the first operational flight of a system designed to restore the country’s sovereign suborbital testing capability. The November 4 launch was conducted from the Directorate General of Armaments’ (DGA) missile test center in Biscarrosse. The launch carried an experimental payload for the French military, supporting research linked to the development of its M51.4 strategic missile.SyLEx stands for Système de Lancement d’Expériences, or Experimental Launch System. Built by ArianeGroup under the direction of the DGA, it is designed to carry experimental equipment to altitudes of 200 to 400 kilometers (124 to 248 miles). The flight followed an initial demonstration on November 28, 2025, making this the system’s second successful launch.French Minister of the Armed Forces and Veterans Catherine Vautrin said the latest mission enabled experiments considered essential to the development of the M51.4 missile. A platform for high-altitude experimentsUnlike orbital launch vehicles, sounding rockets follow suborbital trajectories, carrying instruments and experimental payloads to high altitudes before returning to Earth. They provide researchers with access to atmospheric conditions and short periods of microgravity, making them useful for testing materials, sensors, and other technologies.According to ArianeGroup, SyLEx can carry payloads weighing up to 600 kilograms, with multiple experiments accommodated on a single flight depending on the mission configuration. The system is designed for both military and civilian applications, including atmospheric re-entry research and microgravity experiments.SyLEx comprises two rocket configurations. A single-stage and a two-stage version, supported by a dedicated launch pad. The November 4 mission used the single-stage configuration. ArianeGroup said it is now working with the DGA on the next development milestone: the two-stage version.Reportedly, the single-stage setup supports up to 300 kg (661 pounds) of research equipment.Supporting France’s strategic weapons programsThe latest launch is particularly significant for France’s nuclear deterrent. The M51 family of submarine-launched ballistic missiles forms the sea-based component of the country’s nuclear forces. The M51.4 is a planned evolution of the missile system, although French officials have not disclosed the specific experiments conducted aboard SyLEx or how they will contribute to its development.Vautrin also highlighted the rocket’s potential to support hypersonic demonstrators. High-altitude experimental flights can help evaluate technologies under demanding flight conditions, including those relevant to atmospheric re-entry and high-speed flight. However, the exact hypersonic research activities planned for SyLEx have not been detailed.Une nouvelle avancée pour notre dissuasion !Cette nuit, la @DGA a réalisé avec succès, depuis le site Landes à Biscarosse du centre d’essais et d’expertise DGA Essais de missiles, un tir expérimental de la fusée-sonde française SyLEx (système de lancement d’expériences),… pic.twitter.com/Pdg0R6Mskp— Catherine Vautrin (@CaVautrin) November 4, 2026ArianeGroup described the successful launch as a demonstration of its ability to provide a sovereign suborbital testing platform for major development programs. The company said it developed the system in less than three years for the DGA, the program’s contracting authority.Beyond defense, SyLEx could support civilian research and other European applications. Its payload capacity and ability to accommodate multiple experiments offer a platform for scientific investigations that require access to high altitudes.For France, the launch marks the return of a domestic capability for suborbital flights and high-altitude testing after several decades without one. With the single-stage version now through its first operational flight, the next step is developing the two-stage configuration, which could expand the range of missions the system can undertake.

title: NASA unveils 10,000-pound test aircraft designed to fly at 45,000 feet
content: NASA just revealed the newest member of its iconic X-plane family. On Wednesday, the space agency showcased its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP.Summit at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Compared to static flight-test rigs or single-purpose demonstrators, the X-70 is built around a single, ambitious vision: adaptable speed. It is a crewed, modular flying laboratory designed to rapidly swap experiments and push aircraft maneuverability beyond anything NASA has flown before. The plane bridges decades of flight history with the future. If all goes as planned, NASA plans to launch the aircraft on its maiden flight within the next two years.Built for flexibilityAt first glance, the specs reveal a high-performance workhorse. Weighing in at a 10,000-pound takeoff weight, the aircraft will be able to cruise at Mach 0.75, climb to 45,000 feet, and cover more than 1,726 miles (1,500 nautical miles) on a single run.What really sets the Fractal apart is the technology housed within it. Or rather, what you can swap out.The X-70 can carry up to 2,000 pounds of experimental payloads spread across internal and external mounting locations. Paired with rapidly reconfigurable flight-control tech, engineers won’t have to redesign an entire plane every time they want to test a new aerodynamic concept. They can plug it into the X-70 and take off.“Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next. We expect her first flight under the NASA banner within the next two years, and X-70 is just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics. This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.NASA’s X-70 Fractal provides a reconfigurable testbed for next-generation flight controls that could redefine aircraft agility. Notably, engineers can evaluate morphing wings that change shape in flight alongside targeted thrust vectoring to direct engine exhaust for tight maneuvering. Tests may also explore lift-fan systems for short-takeoff capability or active flow control, which steers the aircraft using precise air jets to replace mechanical flaps entirely.A new chapter for X-planesThe X-70 enters a historic family.America’s aviation legacy was forged on experimental “X-planes“. The Bell X-1 shattered the sound barrier in 1947. The X-15 pushed the frontiers of hypersonic flight. More recently, the X-59 has taken on the challenge of quiet supersonic transit. Now, the X-70 Fractal takes its turn.“The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” added Isaacman.He noted that the aircraft’s modular nature will keep teams learning and moving quickly between tests.Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate, stated that bringing on another X-plane will significantly accelerate aeronautics research. NASA expects the X-70 Fractal to make its inaugural flight under the agency’s banner within the next two years.

title: US nuclear fusion reactor drive taps advanced plasma tech in new deal
content: Fusion energy has long promised virtually limitless, low-carbon power by mimicking the physical reactions that fuel the Sun. But turning laboratory experiments into working power stations remains a huge problem. Connecting that power to the electrical grid is one of science’s greatest engineering challenges.Now, an international pact aims to bridge that divide. Engineering firm Amentum has agreed to a strategic partnership with Japanese developer Kyoto Fusioneering. Under a new agreement, the two companies plan to combine their technical resources. Together, they will focus their work across Japan, the United States, and the United Kingdom. Their shared ambition is straightforward, which is to move fusion from experimental physics rigs into commercially viable power plants.Building a commercial reactor is fundamentally a systems challenge. Reactors require specialized internal hardware that can endure conditions hotter than the solar core. Combining industrial engineering with digital innovationKyoto Fusioneering supplies several of these critical technologies. These include plasma heating devices, advanced fuel-cycle equipment, and “breeding blankets” designed to generate tritium fuel within the reactor walls. Amentum, by contrast, brings the nuclear safety protocols, systems engineering, and large-scale delivery management needed to construct actual industrial facilities.“Building a fusion power plant will depend on collaborations like this one,” said Kiyoshi Seko, president and chief operating officer of Kyoto Fusioneering. He noted that Amentum provides the scale of nuclear engineering experience that developers urgently need as projects advance toward physical construction.A major focus of the venture will be digital simulation. The teams intend to deploy artificial intelligence and digital engineering tools to model plant operations. In theory, testing virtual designs will cut down development cycles, predict equipment degradation, and avoid costly trial-and-error during physical builds.The agreement comes amid rising momentum in Japan. Tokyo’s national fusion strategy has channeled substantial public backing into private demonstration ventures, giving firms like Kyoto Fusioneering a springboard to pursue joint ventures across western markets.“This collaboration comes at a pivotal moment,” said Mark Whitney, president of Amentum’s energy and environment division, arguing that combining their specialisms will directly tackle the delivery hurdles stalling commercial deployment.Extreme testing and reactor hardware trialsThe initiative builds on Kyoto Fusioneering’s growing international testing footprint. In October, the company joined forces with the DIII-D National Fusion Facility in California, a testbed backed by the US Department of Energy.Inside a fusion tokamak, operators face a brutal thermal dilemma. The core plasma must stay searingly hot for atomic nuclei to fuse, but the surrounding chamber walls must stay cool enough to avoid structural failure.To help resolve this, Kyoto Fusioneering is supplying heat-resistant tiles for an advanced “divertor”—the exhaust component that expels waste heat and impurities from the plasma chamber. Alongside researchers from Columbia University, engineers will run extended operational tests on DIII-D’s reverse-D-shaped plasma.Data gathered from those California trials will feed directly into US Department of Energy roadmaps. The measurements will help physicists assess plasma stability, validate computer models, and choose the resilient materials required for the world’s next generation of pilot plants.

title: Unitree G1 humanoid suffers 'heatstroke' on mountain climb in China
content: A Unitree G1 humanoid robot overheated and had to be carried down Mount Taishan on a stretcher during a robot competition in China. The incident occurred during the inaugural CMG World Robot Mount Taishan Competition in Shandong Province of China.Unitree later suggested that the robot may have entered the competition without proper tuning, sparking online debate about humanoid robot endurance and their ability to operate in demanding real-world environments.Recently, the robotics firm demonstrated its G1 humanoid autonomously sparring with a human using its UnifoLM-X2-1.0 AI model, showcasing advances in real-time robotic control.Humanoid endurance testedThe Chinese humanoid robot faced an endurance challenge after overheating during a competitive climb up Mount Taishan on November 2, highlighting the technical difficulties of operating bipedal machines for extended periods on demanding terrain.The G1 development version, also used in China’s Spring Festival Gala, overheated during the race, and its operator had to withdraw it. Event staff subsequently placed the humanoid on a stretcher and carried it down the mountain.The competition offered a demanding test of the robot’s mobility, balance, and thermal management systems. The course covered approximately 3.9 kilometers (2.4 miles), running from Hongmen to Zhongtianmen, with more than 3,100 steps and an elevation gain of around 600 meters (1,970 feet). Unlike demonstrations on flat indoor surfaces, the route required the humanoid to navigate uneven terrain and repeated stair climbs while maintaining its balance, Global Times reported. According to experts, such conditions place considerable demands on a humanoid robot’s mechanical and electronic systems. Walking involves continuous coordination between its joints, actuators, sensors, and onboard control systems. Climbing thousands of steps adds further demands, requiring repeated adjustments to leg movements, body posture, and balance as the robot negotiates elevation changes.Thermal management is another important consideration during sustained operation. Motors, actuators, computing hardware and power electronics generate heat while performing demanding tasks. If the heat produced exceeds the system’s ability to dissipate it, internal temperatures can rise and affect operating reliability. The incident therefore raised questions about how well humanoid robots can manage heat during prolonged physical activity rather than short demonstrations.G1 faces scrutinyUnitree suggested that the G1 development version may have entered the competition without tuning. The company did not provide further technical details about the overheating incident or identify the specific component responsible for the temperature increase.The robot’s withdrawal also prompted discussion about the distinction between demonstrating mobility and sustaining it under demanding conditions. A humanoid may successfully walk, run, or perform complex movements for relatively short periods, but maintaining those capabilities over extended operations requires reliable coordination between its mechanical hardware, control software, and thermal management systems.According to analysts, the Mount Taishan competition exposed these challenges in the field. The combination of thousands of steps, sustained movement, and significant elevation changes provided a different test from the controlled conditions typically used for laboratory demonstrations. It also highlighted the importance of evaluating robots beyond their ability to complete individual movements.The incident does not necessarily indicate a fundamental limitation of the G1 platform, particularly given Unitree’s suggestion that the development model may not have been properly tuned for the event. However, it illustrates why endurance, thermal stability, and adaptability are becoming important measures of humanoid robot performance.
